readout_other: cortical LFP (wPLI functional connectivity, graph theory); gait analysis; TTC infarct staining
direction_notes: After 7 days of TUS, gait indices recovered faster than sham and cortical network connectivity shifted toward the healthy pattern; effect persisted to Day 14 and weakened by Day 21.
safety_notes: Mechanical index calculated as about 0.19 and theoretical temperature rise about 0.0008 C; no adverse-event assessment reported.

timing.protocol_description: FF 1 MHz; PRF 1 Hz; pulse train duration 5 min; DC 5%; PD 50 ms; interstimulus interval 5 min; stimulation once daily for 15 min, for 7 consecutive days starting on Day 1 after stroke.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The animals were randomly divided into three groups (N= 11 per group): poststroke ultrasound stimulation group (stroke + TUS), poststroke sham stimulation group (stroke + sham), and normal mouse group.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: mice were subjected to either TUS intervention or sham stimulation intervention for $7$ consecutive days starting from Day 1 (D1)

flags.reason: Target is described only as the infarct area (distal MCA occlusion, right hemisphere); cortex term chosen by inference from the model.
33 mice in three groups of 11; 11 received TUS (stroke + TUS group).
Pressure measured with a hydrophone behind the skull; the Discussion says ex vivo skull. Isppa and Ispta were calculated by the authors from it.
Pulse train 5 min with 5 min ISI within a 15 min daily session; PRF 1 Hz with PD 50 ms gives 5 % as stated.
Sham stimulation mechanism not described; normal group received no stimulation.
TUNSS-1 is the driving device; transducer maker is Olympus.
